transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-12
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 45m
Attendees: Eli Navarro (Redwood AE), Priya Menon (Redwood SE), Carlos Vega (Redwood SE twitch?), Marina Duval (Aphelion Head of ML), Jonas Richter (CTO), Leah Ortiz (Compliance), Sasha Kim (PM)

Summary: quick intake to understand Aphelion's budget constraints, residency/compliance needs, and whether Hosted, Dedicated or Private is the right path. Focus on per-token economics, batching/caching levers, and pilot scope.

Topics: budget cap, traffic shape and spikes, latency targets, data residency, SOC2/KMS, POC success criteria, timeline to decision.

[00:00] Eli Navarro: hey everyone thanks for joining — can you hear me okay?
[00:05] Marina Duval: yep, loud and clear, thanks Eli.
[00:10] Jonas Richter: good to go. short on time so appreciate the agenda.

[00:20] Eli Navarro: cool. quick intro — I'm Eli, AE on infra and cost side, Priya is our SE who focuses on batching, caching and private deployments. we'll kick off with a 10 minute intake on what you're trying to build, then go into economics and options.
[00:40] Priya Menon: hi all, great to be here. quick note: i'll be calling out effective tokens, cache hit assumptions, and rough latency tradeoffs.

[01:00] Sasha Kim: for context we're Aphelion, we do automated legal summarization for EU customers — so residency and audit logs are important. our target is a 99th percentile latency under 1.2s for short summaries (~200 tokens) for interactive product. budget is tight: initial monthly spend can't exceed \u20ac12k.

[01:25] Leah Ortiz: and compliance — we need SOC2 compliance, audit logs, and keys managed via our KMS. if private deployment is needed we need to understand onsite options or VPC peering.

[01:40] Eli Navarro: great, that's helpful. couple clarifying qs then we'll map options to unit economics. first, traffic shape — average requests per minute and peak bursts?
[01:52] Marina Duval: baseline 3–5 rps during business hours, peaks up to 30 rps for a few hours after market/legal filings. monthly tokens estimate ~8–12M tokens.

[02:10] Priya Menon: and what's your prompt size and average response length? you said ~200 tokens final — what's the input?
[02:18] Marina Duval: inputs range 60–180 tokens; output we cap at 200 normally, sometimes 400 for deep case summaries.

[02:30] Eli Navarro: ok. cost model overview: Hosted is simplest — per-token charges, we already publish typical per-1k-token rates but effective unit cost depends on batching and cache hit rates. Dedicated gives reserved capacity (predictable throughput) with lower per-token inference cost but a monthly commitment. Private (VPC/on-prem) addresses residency and KMS control but adds infra ops overhead and often larger commit or license.

[03:05] Jonas Richter: can you quantify — ballpark per-token on hosted vs dedicated for a model like ours? and how much do batching and caching move that?

[03:18] Priya Menon: happy to. for a 7B/13B-class open model used for summarization, hosted list pricing is \u20ac0.40–0.70 per 1k prompt tokens and \u20ac0.40–0.70 per 1k completion tokens (varies by model). effective per-inference cost for a 200-token completion with 120-token prompt is 320 tokens; at \u20ac0.6/1k that's ~\u20ac0.192 per call. with batching and a 20% KV/prefix cache hit we can reduce token generation by ~15–30% and amortize GPU overhead giving ~10–20% lower effective cost.

[04:00] Priya Menon: Dedicated reserved capacity usually drops the per-token inference runtime charge by 25–40% depending on utilization. but you pay for reserved pool whether you use it or not; so if you have sustained traffic (your 8–12M/mo is promising) dedicated often makes sense.

[04:20] Marina Duval: our constraint is the \u20ac12k monthly cap for the pilot. how would that map to tokens?

[04:30] Eli Navarro: at \u20ac0.6 per 1k tokens naive hosted-only math gives ~20M tokens per month at \u20ac12k. but that's raw tokens; effective tokens are lower when you add system tokens (system prompts, safety checks), and you may not achieve ideal cache/batching on day 1. safe planning say 12–15M effective tokens.

[04:55] Jonas Richter: you mentioned spikes — if we get a 30 rps spike that could blow the budget if not throttled. what are throttles/fallbacks?

[05:05] Priya Menon: Redwood has routing policies and fallback variants — we can route traffic to lower-cost model variants under burst, or queue/serve partially cached responses. Also per-route quotas. That helps keep budget predictable.

[05:25] Marina Duval: curious about KV cache — our use-case has a lot of repeated legal boilerplate, could caching help?

[05:33] Priya Menon: yes — prefix caching is often effective for doc-based summarization. if the prompt prefixes reoccur, your cache hit could be 20–40% which directly reduces token generation. operationally we can size the KV cache and set TTLs for sensitive content. note: cache eviction patterns matter for bursty workloads.

[06:00] Eli Navarro: also worth thinking about model quantization and sequence lengths. if you can cap completions at 200 tokens and limit model context, you get better batching density.

[06:14] Leah Ortiz: about residency and KMS — can Hosted support EU-only data residency and customer-managed keys?

[06:22] Eli Navarro: Hosted supports region controls and per-tenant tenancy options; for customer-managed keys, Hosted integrates with KMS partners but if you need full control and on-prem keys, Private or Dedicated with VPC-hosting is recommended.

[06:40] Jonas Richter: we may prefer VPC peering or Private if compliance requires it. but ops cost is a concern. can you share typical costs for Private?

[06:50] Priya Menon: Private pricing is case-by-case. generally Private has platform/license fee + infra estimate. For your scale, Private is usually higher upfront (one-time onboarding + minimum monthly) but allows full control. A middle ground is Redwood Dedicated in EU region with VPC peering and customer-managed KMS which often satisfies compliance while keeping infra ops lower.

[07:20] Sasha Kim: can we run a short pilot hosted first to prove accuracy and caching effects before moving to Dedicated?

[07:28] Eli Navarro: that's a common path. suggested pilot: 6-week hosted pilot with instrumentation, target 10M tokens budget, measure cache-hit, p99 latency, and unit cost. if utilization is steady, move to Dedicated with a 3–6 month reservation to lower per-token cost.

[07:50] Marina Duval: ok that's sensible. question on canary and fallbacks — if we push to a cheaper model under load, do we risk sudden quality regressions?

[07:58] Priya Menon: yes risk exists. Redwood supports A/B tests and progressive rollouts with automatic quality checks vs a held-out prompt set. you define allowed quality delta; if model variant breaches threshold, routing can rollback. we can run initial evals on your prompt set to estimate quality delta.

[08:30] Jonas Richter: about batching — do we need to change our app to batch requests or is it server-side?

[08:38] Priya Menon: both. Redwood runtime does server-side continuous batching, but you get the most benefit if clients coalesce requests (e.g., short-lived clients, queues). we can recommend SDK patterns. for interactive summarization batching is modest but helps during bursts.

[09:05] Marina Duval: what's realistic latency after batching? our p99 target 1.2s for 200-token completion — can you hit that on Hosted?

[09:15] Priya Menon: yes many customers hit ~800–1,000ms p99 for similar workloads on Hosted with low batching depth; Dedicated gives slightly better p99 predictability due to reserved capacity. Private depends on on-prem hardware. we should benchmark with your exact prompts.

[09:35] Eli Navarro: let's run through a few scenarios mapping to your \u20ac12k pilot cap. scenario A: Hosted-only conservative (no cache) — you get ~20M raw tokens but effective maybe 12M after system tokens; scenario B: Hosted with 25% cache/batching gains — maybe ~15–18M effective; scenario C: Dedicated small reserve — upfront monthly commit might be \u20ac8k–10k which could lower per-token cost and give headroom for bursts.

[10:10] Jonas Richter: can Dedicated have burst capacity above commit for spikes?

[10:15] Priya Menon: yes we offer burst capacity add-ons at higher marginal cost and automatic overflow to hosted pool if desired. you can set failover policies to either queue or route to cheaper model.

[10:30] Leah Ortiz: on audit logging — do you provide immutable logs and how long retained?

[10:36] Eli Navarro: Redwood provides request/response metadata logs and optionally full transcripts for debugging; retention configurable per plan. for compliance customers we commonly do 1–7 year retention via S3 integration and immutable retention policies. We can also stream logs into their SIEM.

[10:55] Marina Duval: that helps. for keys we need HSM or customer-managed KMS — is that supported on Dedicated?

[11:02] Priya Menon: yes Dedicated + VPC peering supports customer KMS/HSM integrations; Private is full control. Hosted has KMS partners but not full HSM BYOK in the same way. we'll include the exact matrix in follow-up doc.

[11:20] Sasha Kim: what about evaluation metrics for POC success — what do you recommend?

[11:28] Eli Navarro: recommended pilot success criteria: 1) p99 latency <= 1.2s for 200 token completion under normal load, 2) average unit cost <= pilot target (we'll compute target given budget), 3) cache hit >= 15% within pilot window, 4) no compliance blockers (KMS/audit), 5) acceptable quality delta <= 3% measured by your held-out prompts.

[12:05] Priya Menon: we'll run an initial eval on a sample of your prompts — that gives an estimated per-inference token usage and quality delta. that feeds the budget math.

[12:20] Jonas Richter: ok. can you show a live calc quickly? say 10M monthly tokens, 200 token completions average effective tokens/call 320 — what's calls per month and cost?

[12:33] Priya Menon: 10M tokens / 320 tokens per call ~31.25k calls/mo, at \u20ac0.6/1k tokens => 10M * 0.0006 = \u20ac6,000. so under \u20ac12k cap good headroom. but remember standards: system tokens, safety checks, and retries add ~10–20% overhead. with 20% overhead cost ~\u20ac7,200. with caching/batching you could reduce generation tokens by 15% -> ~\u20ac6,120. Dedicated could drop per-token effective unit further but needs commit.

[13:10] Marina Duval: interesting — so a hosted pilot seems feasible within \u20ac12k. are there other hidden costs?

[13:17] Eli Navarro: additional costs can be observability retention add-ons, long-term private deployment onboarding, or dedicated engineering support. We'll surface those in the pricing sheet.

[13:30] Jonas Richter: about SLA — we need a 99.9% uptime SLA for production later. is that part of Dedicated or add-on?

[13:38] Eli Navarro: SLA options are tied to plan: Hosted has standard SLA; Dedicated gives stronger SLA and enterprise SLAs are available for private deployments. We'll include exact SLO numbers.

[13:55] Leah Ortiz: can we get a sample contract or security pack?

[14:00] Eli Navarro: yes we'll send the security/compliance pack (SOC2, ISO, pen test summaries) and a sample DPA. that's in the follow-up.

[14:10] Marina Duval: what's the timeline if we want to go from pilot to Dedicated — how long to onboard reserved capacity?

[14:18] Priya Menon: typically 2–6 weeks depending on quota and region availability. Dedicated setup includes capacity provisioning, routing policies, and optionally VPC peering which adds a week or two. Private is longer — multi-week with infra planning.

[14:35] Sasha Kim: for the pilot, can we limit exposure by setting per-route quotas and budget alerts?

[14:40] Eli Navarro: absolutely — you can set per-route hard caps, alerting thresholds, and automatic throttles. We'll demonstrate in console during the technical deep-dive.

[14:52] Jonas Richter: a practical ask — show us expected burn per day for different cache hit and batching assumptions. can you model three cases? conservative (0% cache), realistic (20% cache), optimistic (35% cache)?

[15:03] Priya Menon: yes we'll model that. quick back-of-envelope: with 10M tokens and 0% cache cost ~\u20ac6k. realistic 20% -> ~\u20ac4,800. optimistic 35% -> ~\u20ac3,900. we'll put daily burn numbers and p99 latency tradeoffs in the spreadsheet.

[15:30] Marina Duval: perfect. any issues with tokenization differences across models? we sometimes see big variances.

[15:36] Priya Menon: tokenization varies; we'll run your sample through recommended models to estimate tokens precisely — that's part of the eval.

[15:50] Jonas Richter: one more compliance: we need to ensure deletion requests are honored and we can purge logs — is that supported?

[15:57] Eli Navarro: yes we support deletion workflows and can configure log retention and purging policies. for Private deployments you control everything. for Hosted we provide deletion APIs and configurable retention.

[16:15] Sasha Kim: ok next: what does the POC step look like operationally? minimum data we need?

[16:22] Priya Menon: ideal pilot artifacts: sample prompt set (100–200 prompts), representative traffic trace, list of target endpoints and latency targets, and compliance questionnaire. Marina you can redact PII if needed.

[16:40] Marina Duval: we'll send sample prompts and a week's traffic trace.

[16:46] Eli Navarro: great. to recap — recommendation: start with hosted pilot (6 weeks), instrument for cache-hit/latency, then evaluate moving to Dedicated if utilization is sustained to reduce per-token cost. Private considered if strict on-prem or HSM BYOK is mandatory.

[17:05] Jonas Richter: sounds good. could you include the math and burst handling behaviors in the sheet?

[17:11] Eli Navarro: yes — sheet will include scenario math, recommended thresholds for routing, and cost vs latency tradeoffs.

[17:20] Leah Ortiz: we'll need to review the security pack before pilot sign-off.

[17:24] Eli Navarro: noted — we'll attach SOC2/ISO and DPA.

[17:30] Marina Duval: timeline — want to kick pilot end of April if possible.

[17:35] Eli Navarro: we can aim to start 2026-04-27 pending your sample data. next steps: send pricing spreadsheet, batching/caching recommendations, schedule technical deep-dive wk of 2026-04-20.

[17:50] Priya Menon: i'll include a modelling sheet that shows daily burn with variable cache hits and bursts.

[18:00] Sasha Kim: any outstanding blockers?

[18:05] Marina Duval: just internal procurement sign-off but pilot cost is within our expected cap. Leah to confirm compliance pack items.

[18:15] Leah Ortiz: yes i'll review once we have the security docs.

[18:20] Eli Navarro: perfect. thanks everyone. i'll send notes and the spreadsheet, Priya will send configs. we'll follow up to lock the deep-dive.

[18:35] Jonas Richter: thanks all.

[18:40] Meeting end.
